articles.title: Mexico City GP Qualifying: Lewis Hamilton claims first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton claims first grand prix pole position for Ferrari in Mexico City; Hamilton edged out George Russell for first pole since July 2023; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm) to see if Kimi Antonelli can become champion, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Hamilton had been outpaced by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc throughout the weekend but the 41-year-old produced his best lap when it mattered most at the end of Q3 to edge out Russell by nine thousandths of a second.

The seven-time world champion has twice claimed Sprint poles since his move from Mercedes to Ferrari at the start of the 2025 season but will now start a grand prix from the front of the grid for the first time since July 2023 after extending his record tally to 105 poles.

Speaking over team radio after being confirmed as Formula 1's oldest pole-sitter for 44 years, Hamilton said: "Thank you so much, it has been such a long time coming."

Leclerc had led Max Verstappen after the first runs in Q3, but the pair had to settle for third and fourth, respectively, after both making errors on their final efforts.

Kimi Antonelli, who will be crowned F1's youngest ever world champion on Sunday if he finishes ninth or higher, was almost two tenths off the pace in fifth.

Antonelli will start from fourth as a result of Verstappen having been handed a one-place grid penalty for a collision with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson during second practice on Friday.

Lando Norris took sixth for McLaren as his team-mate Oscar Piastri suffered a surprise Q2 exit that leaves the Australian starting 13th.

Isack Hadjar was seventh in the other Red Bull, finishing a place ahead of Lawson, who also drops a position on Sunday's grid for his role in Friday's collision with Verstappen.

His Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad will climb a position to eighth on the grid, while Alpine's Pierre Gasly rounds out the top 10.

Despite appearing to have the pace to advance from Q1, Fernando Alonso exited in the first part of the session after suffering a water pressure issue that caused him to stop on track and resulted in a brief red-flag stoppage.

Ryo Hirakawa was 19th on his F1 qualifying debut having been drafted in to replace Esteban Ocon following a fall out between the French driver and team boss Ayao Komatsu on Friday evening.

Hamilton 'lost for words' after ending pole wait

Not for the first time this season, Ferrari had gone into Saturday as pole favourites after a strong showing on Friday saw Leclerc comfortably top both sessions.

While Ferrari impressed, Hamilton endured a challenging Friday as he lost a big chunk of track time after a technical issue caused him to stop on track in second practice.

Ferrari's advantage appeared to have disappeared overnight when Leclerc was third and Hamilton only sixth in final practice on Saturday, but they returned to form in the opening stages of qualifying.

Hamilton topped Q1, before Verstappen edged both Ferraris in Q2, with Norris actually finishing fastest having used fresh tyres at the end of the period.

Even with Verstappen facing his grid penalty, there was still major uncertainty over whether a Ferrari would start from the front of the grid given the way they have repeatedly fallen away when in contention for pole at recent races.

In keeping with the weekend's form, Leclerc was the faster Ferrari on the first Q3 runs, edging Verstappen by 0.045s, with an error in the middle sector leaving Hamilton four tenths off the pace in fourth.

However, it was all change on the second runs, with Russell coming from nowhere to momentarily take provisional pole, before Hamilton bettered him by the smallest of margins with his time of 1:16.514s to go fastest.

Leclerc was next up, but this time was unable to hook up his lap and only marginally improved on his previous effort to remain more than a tenth back from Hamilton.

Verstappen was up on Hamilton after two sectors, but locked up in the slow-speed final part of the lap after coming up behind Norris, with the Dutchman saying the presence of the McLaren meant he lost his braking reference.

That confirmed Hamilton's first pole since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, leading to joyous celebrations from F1's record race-winner as he clenched both fists after exiting the cockpit before running into the arms of his mechanics.

Speaking moments later, Hamilton said: "That felt great! That feels good! I'm so happy. I'm lost for words. It's been a really challenging weekend.

"It feels special to be here in Mexico and [pole position] 105, I like that number."

articles.title: Mexico City Grand Prix qualifying result: Lewis Hamilton takes pole position
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton takes his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has claimed his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The seven-time F1 champion beat Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds as the two drivers who can potentially stop Kimi Antonelli clinching the world title on Sunday locked out the front row.

Antonelli qualified fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, but will start fourth because of a one-place penalty for the Dutchman.

The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and the Italian finishes lower than ninth, or if Hamilton wins and Antonelli is out of the points.

Hamilton's pole is his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, three years and three months ago, and the 105th of his career.

He is the oldest driver to secure a pole since Mario Andretti for Ferrari at the 1982 Italian Grand Prix.

He and Russell both went out early for their first runs and had to watch as their rivals sought and failed to beat them.

Leclerc went first, falling short of Hamilton by 0.119secs. Antonelli was never on target but Verstappen was fastest of all after two sectors and on course to take pole.

But the Dutchman locked up into the hairpin in the stadium section and ruined his lap.

"Oh man, I'm lost for words," said Hamilton. "It's been a really challenging weekend - we had the engine issue yesterday, which meant we were on the back foot and didn't do a long run.

"We've done a really good job on the setup and to have pole here, wow, it feels special. It's my first pole for Ferrari, and 105th, I like that number.

"To have your first Ferrari pole, it takes me back to watching Michael [Schumacher] get all those poles when he was at Ferrari and all those wins."

Hamilton had been only fourth on the first runs, more than 0.4secs off Leclerc's pace-setting time. But on his final run, he said: "I don't think I lost any time anywhere. It was a super-good lap."

F1 has never had anyone like me - Hamilton

How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC

Russell, who said he was happy to have ended a run of difficult form but could not explain why, took a unilateral decision not to do a preparation lap after his out lap on his final run.

He said he had a "gut feeling" that it was the best approach, but the team had insisted on a prep lap and had fuelled the car for the extra mileage.

"[The time loss for the extra fuel weight is] such a small number," said Russell, "but it's bigger than the gap to pole. Nevertheless, I'm just happy to be up here."

Verstappen said traffic with another car is what led to his loss of time.

"Already going into (Turn) 12 I had a car very close to me and I already lost time there with the dirty air," he said.

"And then going into the hairpin, instead of going on the left, I had one car on my right where you normally want to open up the corner. So its a bit of an awkward angle you have to go into the hairpin.

"Plus you lose your reference on the right-hand side where you are constantly looking. It's a difficult corner to get right, that killed my lap. The most promising thing is how we turned it around as in practice I was not that happy and we turned it around, I was in the fight for pole."

McLaren's Lando Norris had looked in contention for pole, fastest in the second session and on the first runs in the final session, when he was third fastest behind Leclerc and Verstappen.

But he failed to improve on his final lap and had to be satisfied fight sixth.

"Just not quick enough that's all," said Norris. "The lap was incredible in Q2 to put me P1. That was very unrealistic in terms of achieving that again in Q3.

"I am pretty happy with P6, can't ask a lot more and pretty happy with the job I did with the car I have."

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls pair Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completed the top 10.

Fernando Alonso looked to be in contention for his best qualifying of the year for Aston Martin when he went fastest on his first lap of the session ahead of a number of cars that for most of the season have been ahead of him.

But his engine suffered a water leak in the energy recovery system as he started his second attempt, when he was still lying third, and he was ordered to stop the car on track.

Alonso's frustration after a year of poor performance and reliability from the Honda engine was clear in an interview with the official television channel afterwards, when he said a total of nine words in answer to four questions.

In those words, he confirmed it had been an engine problem, said "it was" a good opportunity and it was "correct" that the car has been looking good all weekend - but that he could not do anything in the race "from the back".

articles.standfirst: Un problema mecánico en el Aston Martin revienta cualquier opción del asturiano en el que se perfilaba como el mejor Gran Premio de la temporada
articles.summary: Un problema mecánico en el Aston Martin revienta cualquier opción del asturiano en el que se perfilaba como el mejor Gran Premio de la temporada
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton sigue haciendo historia. El británico no superará en 2026 los siete títulos de Michael Schumacher, pero su carrera eterna acumula más registros únicos. De esos que parecen inalcanzables, de esos que hablan de una carrera legendaria. En México logró su pole 105 tras una clasificación de vértigo y saldrá primero a una carrera (21:00 horas, DAZN) que no tenía reservada la fiesta a su nombre. Eso pertenece a Andrea Kimi Antonelli, cuarto en parrilla y con un noveno como límite para convertirse en el campeón más joven de la historia de la Fórmula 1. Antonelli sólo tiene que limitar riesgos y pensar en pasar las vueltas, pero no queda descartado. Se beneficia del castigo a Verstappen por la macarrada con Lawson del viernes (cae al quinto), y esperará acontecimientos justo detrás de sus principales rivales. Hamilton está en la pole y Russell a su lado buscando un triunfo que compense su bajón según ha avanzado la temporada 2026. La pesadilla correspondió, de nuevo, para Fernando Alonso. Se había perfilado el mejor fin de semana de la temporada y la lucha por la Q3 era legítima, pero el Aston Martin volvió a fallar. Tras marcar un primer tiempo, el coche dio malas sensaciones en el cambio de marchas, empezó a salir humo y desde el muro verde pidieron frenar al bicampeón. "Páralo ya", decía su ingeniero ante un incrédulo Fernando. "No se ha roto nada", explicaba sin saber el problema real. Parece relacionado a la presión del agua. El fallo mecánico le enviará al final de la parrilla (puesto 17 por el castigo a Bortoleto). Algo mejor partirá Carlos Sainz, que entró en Q2 tras una batalla ante Albon que sigue dominando en el cara a cara. No pasa del 15 y es el rendimiento máximo que su Williams puede dar. Sigue muy difícil, se quedó a un segundo del Haas de Bearman y dependerá de un jaleo que siempre existe en la Ciudad de México. El segundo corte era todo lo que podía dar en sábado, lugar en el que también se quedó un Piastri desastroso (13º). "No tengo grip", decía el australiano. La fiesta del domingo apunta a Antonelli. Que sale de la zona sucia y encarará una primera curva peligrosa, pero también tiene un margen amplísimo sobre unos rivales que controlará en la distancia. Sabe que el noveno llegará con casi terminar, y la victoria puede esperar ante una competencia que quiere volver a respirar ante el tirano boloñés. La encabeza Hamilton. El británico levantó a Ferrari en sábado, pues no habían logrado pole alguna en toda la campaña (sí Mercedes, Red Bull, McLaren y Alpine) y necesitaba ese empujón para volver a salir primero. Lo logró al sobrevivir a una vuelta infernal, de baja adherencia y donde todos los demás cometieron pequeños errores. Sólo pilotó limpio, sin perder el Ferrari y metiendo a sus rivales tiempo por pura consistencia. Le ocurrió al bestial Verstappen tras dos sectores de locos, también a Leclerc aunque parte tercero y puede atacar. Y el 44 supo sostener el pulso con un Russell que perdió su ventaja en un parcial final letal si los neumáticos se caen. Poco menos de una décima les separó. De cara al domingo, su camino se despeja, aunque rematar es la palabra más difícil de las que componen el vocabulario de la F1. La batalla promete emociones fuertes. No se descarta la aparición de Norris desde atrás (sexto) y las primeras curvas pueden tragarse muchas opciones. Lo que es seguro es la fuerza de Hamilton, su búsqueda permanente de la historia... y el paso a la corona necesario de un Antonelli que vivirá su gran día.

articles.title: Un Alonso roto: "La frustración es indescriptible"
articles.standfirst: Es 18º, cuando iba a luchar por los 10 mejores según cree. Una avería en la refrigeración de la batería acabó con sus opciones. Es posible que cambie motor
articles.summary: Es 18º, cuando iba a luchar por los 10 mejores según cree. Una avería en la refrigeración de la batería acabó con sus opciones. Es posible que cambie motor
articles.body: Fernando Alonso estaba en una de su mejores calificaciones del año, donde en su primer intento estaba cerca de pasar a la Q2, cuando al entrar en boxes para el segundo le ordenaban que parase su coche antes de la entrada al pit lane. Se vio humo y se detectó una bajada de presión de agua en la zona que refrigera el ERS (Sistema de recuperación de energía), una zona crítica por ser la de las baterías y el generados MGU-K. Y pese a parar, no está garantizado que puedan salvar esa unidad. Lo más probable, como reconocía Fernando es que le cambien parte para la carrera de mañana. "Estaba a 100 metros del garaje, pero probablemente el problema era demasiado grave como para poder solucionarlo allí. Así que, bueno, lo más seguro para todos los demás que estaban en pista era parar, y seguí las instrucciones", relataba. "El problema estaba en el motor", dijo sin más detalles. Y el español creía que llegar a la Q3 hubiera sido posible: "Habría sido difícil, pero sí. Estábamos en la posición 12, 13 u 11, así que estábamos dentro del margen. Si hubiéramos hecho una buena vuelta, quizás habría sido posible, aunque creo que eso sería ser demasiado optimista. Probablemente, nuestra posición real hoy era la 12ª o 13ª", concedía. Para Alonso, que reconoce que estaba "ilusionado", el fin de semana no es recuperable ya. "No, no, no. Todos tenemos graves problemas con las temperaturas. Cuando sales desde atrás, es imposible seguir a otros coches de cerca. Así que no hay mucho que podamos hacer. Creo que hemos perdido una gran oportunidad, la frustración es indescriptible. Pero bueno, esa ha sido la tónica de todo el año", lamentaba. El buen rendimiento del coche en México se debe a que, "hay menos rectas. Solo hay dos: la que lleva a la curva 1 y la que lleva a la 4. En el resto del circuito, con un nivel de agarre tan bajo, apenas puedes ir a fondo. Por tanto, el coche depende menos de la potencia del motor. Quizás sea por eso", valoraba. Fernando reconocía que quizá deba cambiar el motor y haya penalización. "La verdad es que no lo sé. Supongo que sí", decía decepcionado.

articles.summary: Antonelli tendrá que luchar para ganar 'a lo campeón'
articles.body: ¡Qué cerca tiene Antonelli el título! El piloto italiano lo tiene todo alineado para poder llevarse en México el Mundial de F1, consagrándose así como el más joven de la historia en hacerlo, batiendo al mismísimo Vettel y cerrando, a falta de 4 citas más, una temporada prácticamente perfecta. No obstante, que esté muy seguro no quiere decir que vaya a ser fácil, pues hay muchos gallos a su alrededor que quieren llevarse una de las pocas victorias que quedan. A pesar de haber dominado el fin de semana Charles Leclerc, fue el otro Ferrari quien se llevó la 'Pole' del Gran Premio de México, seguido de Russell y del monegasco. Verstappen y Norris, quienes parecían poder poner algo más de "picante", fallaron en la vuelta importante, y tan sólo pudieron clasificar 4º el neerlandés, con una posición de parrilla de sanción por su incidente con Lawson durante los Libres 2, y 6º el británico. Entre medias, y que por lo tanto se ve beneficiado por la sanción a Verstappen, es, precisamente, el líder del Mundial, Kimi Antonelli que, definitivamente tendrá que luchar si quiere ganar a lo campeón. La buenas sensaciones de Fernando Alonso durante todo el fin de semana, estando mucho más cerca de lo que ha estado durante la temporada, hasta la Q1, donde el asturiano tuvo un problema de presión del agua en su coche, relacionado con el ERS (sistema eléctrico), lo cual se supone que era el circuito que refrigeraba la batería. Así pues, Alonso tuvo que abandonar la sesión y partirá el domingo en carrera desde la 18ª posición. Mientras, Carlos Sainz, quien parecía tener un finde más desastroso, comparado al del asturiano, pudo pasar a Q2 por los pelos pero, de nuevo, la realidad de su Williams le volvió a golpear y un 1.18.885 que no fue suficiente para pasar el corte. articles.title: Horse racing: Ryan Moore wins Breeders' Cup Turf for record time with Benvenuto Cellini
articles.summary: Jockey Ryan Moore and trainer Aidan O'Brien both made history as they won the Breeders' Cup Turf with Benvenuto Cellini.
articles.body:
Ryan Moore won the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland for a record sixth time on Saturday in Kentucky.

The English jockey triumphed in the £3.7m ($5m) feature race with Benvenuto Cellini, timing his final push perfectly and powering home by three-quarters of a lenght ahead of compatriot James Doyle on Map Of Stars in second.

It gave Irish trainer Aidan O'Brien a record-extending eighth victory in the race, with another of his horses Diamond Necklace finishing in third.

Moore was appointed MBE for services to racing and British sport in June, is widely regarded as the best jockey of his generation and rode Estimate to victory in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot in 2013 for Queen Elizabeth II.

O'Brien, who was equalling his own record of 28 top-level victories in a calendar year, praised his horse, who was 3-1 favourite.

"He's a horse that showed a lot of class. Ryan was calm and relaxed on him and let it happen. He was brilliant on him. He did it again, he had to come out and come round," he said.

"Time after time he produces on the day. He accepted early he let them go, but he had one bullet to fire which he executed perfectly."

"It's so special that everyone is here. It's a special day."

Benvenuto Cellini's dam Newspaperofrecord herself won the Breeders' Cup in 2018.

In the Breeders' Cup Classic, Venezuelan jockey Junior Alvarado won with Sovereignty.

The four-year-old horse was scrapped from competing last year because of fever, but swept aside the competition including Japan's Forever Young who was going for his second successive win but finished in fifth.

Trained by American Bill Mott, Alvarado said his victory with Sovereignty was "spectacular".

"We really wanted to run so bad the Classic last year. I'm just so glad the Godolphin team gave us a chance to keep him in training and get to do what he did today," he said.

articles.title: Mexico City Grand Prix: Esteban Ocon denies reports of physical altercation behind Haas dropping
articles.summary: Esteban Ocon denies reports that his being dropped by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix was a consequence of a row with team principal Ayao Komatsu descending into a physical confrontation.
articles.body:
Esteban Ocon has denied reports that his being dropped by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix was a consequence of a row with team principal Ayao Komatsu descending into a physical confrontation.

The Frenchman, 30, admitted in a statement on social media that "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved".

But he said he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature".

His statement followed a report in France's L'Equipe , external which said that a meeting between Komatsu and Ocon "ended abruptly, perhaps even physically".

The decision to stand Ocon down from the rest of the Mexico weekend came after he had had a dispute with race engineer Laura Mueller about tyre choice during second practice on Friday.

Mueller had informed him that plans to run the soft-compound tyre had been changed and he would now use the medium.

He replied: "No, no. I want to do soft... don't do that to me, come on."

The team have not issued any further information what happened after the session.

So far, Haas have only said that Ocon has been dropped for this weekend's race.

The team announced last month that he would be leaving Haas at the end of the season. He is being replaced by the Brazilian Rafael Camara, leader of the Formula 2 championship and a member of the Ferrari driver development programme.

Neither Haas not sources within Ocon's management have commented on whether Ocon will drive for Haas again at any of this year's remaining races.

Ocon's statement on Saturday continued: "I strongly condemn violence in all its forms and firmly believe that disagreements should always be handled with professionalism, respect, and mutual understanding.

"I kindly ask that speculation be avoided while the matter is being addressed. Further updates will be communicated in due course."

articles.body: El deporte son emociones, son sentimientos, es el trabajo bien hecho el día en el que importa el cuándo y el dónde. Y uno importante es el del Gran Premio de México (21:00 horas, DAZN) porque Lewis Hamilton saldrá desde su pole 105 (el que más) buscando la victoria 107 (el que más también). Y Andrea Kimi Antonelli tiene ante sí la mayor gloria, la de cerrar una corona que reventará los libros de historia. A Antonelli le vale con un noveno y sale cuarto, algo positivo y que le deja el camino despejado. Pero no oculta que quizá hay un factor más en este fin de semana: el de ganar. Ya no lo oculta. “Fue complicado, creo que me faltó confianza. Estoy más tenso que en otras ocasiones”, confesó. De cualquier forma, el remate es el más sencillo aunque sus dos rivales, Hamilton y Russell, partirán en cabeza. Con un foco en el británico, al que une una historia común con Kimi. Ha repetido que le admira y valora su título. También heredó su lugar y equipo en Mercedes, y Hamilton sabía desde el inicio que era el sucesor natural. También puede entrar en la fiesta a su manera, con una primera posición en parrilla para disfrutar. “Esperé mucho para vivir este momento, cuando tienes la voluntad siempre encuentras el camino”, reconocía con emoción. Nadie le quitaba la sonrisa y esa satisfacción al casi abrazar a su Ferrari. Ante sí tendrá el reto más grande y loco, pues la recta del Hermanos Rodríguez es un lugar en el que siempre hay caos. De hecho, la FIA ya ha advertido a los equipos para que se comporten sus pilotos pues no permitirán ganar ventaja fuera los límites. El riesgo existirá y Hamilton se encontrará con Russell, su compañero Leclerc, el lanzado Antonelli y saben que tarde o temprano llegará Verstappen. Para el título, algo similar. Kimi debe salvar la papeleta y volver a un ritmo que abra camino, aunque quizá la presión que antes no existía también le pone pimienta al asunto. “No está siendo sencillo. No es fácil mantenerme estable de emociones. Y quizá estoy más tenso, eso es un gran factor. Pero intentaré aprovechar esta noche con mi familia y amigos, y después enfocarme”, finalizó. Su sueño está ahí, ya sólo tiene que agarrarlo con las dos manos.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton enjoys Mexico City Grand Prix pole as Kimi Antonelli aims to clinch title
articles.summary: As Kimi Antonelli bids to become F1's youngest world champion, veteran Lewis Hamilton rolled back the years to take his first Ferrari pole.
articles.body:
So far, Kimi Antonelli has been a wallflower at his own party at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Fourth place on the grid is low-key for the Mercedes driver in the context of his season as a whole - and the gargantuan achievement of which he stands on the brink.

It still puts the 20-year-old Italian in a strong position to seal the maiden title that will make him the youngest champion in history.

But on Saturday that was overshadowed by the veteran whose seat Antonelli took at Mercedes, as Lewis Hamilton secured his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years.

The seven-time champion edged out his former Mercedes team-mate George Russell by just 0.009 seconds to clinch his first pole since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix and the 105th of his stellar career.

Fittingly, the only two drivers who, at least mathematically, can prevent Antonelli from sealing the deal on Sunday are together on the front row.

The only possible way in which Antonelli will not become champion at the end of the race is if either Hamilton or Russell win. Even then, he needs only to finish ninth if it's Russell or 10th if it's Hamilton to be sure.

Hamilton said the idea was not even in his mind.

"That's not really something we're thinking of," he said. "We're thinking of just trying to score the best result for the team.

"Kimi, he's continued to drive really well and doing what he needs to do. All he has to do is just finish where he is, and he's kind of on his own journey.

"Our journey is to focus on performing the best we can this weekend and holding on to second in the Constructors' Championship."

Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix

F1 has never had anyone like me - Hamilton

How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC

Russell said it was "obviously inevitable" that Antonelli would win the championship, adding that it would be "most likely this weekend".

He continued: "So, for me personally, just going out there to try to have a good race. I want to try to finish this season strong. That's the biggest priority for me.

"In my mind, he's kind of already won the championship. So that's something that I don't think I need to deal with."

Antonelli, though, would not agree with Hamilton's assessment of his weekend so far.

He has looked quick at times, but in qualifying it did not come together, and he ended up 0.184secs off Russell. He was fifth fastest, but a one-place penalty for Red Bull's Max Verstappen puts Antonelli on the second row alongside Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc.

Antonelli admitted that the high stakes of the weekend were on his mind, to the extent that it was affecting his driving.

"I just feel like I didn't do a good enough job out there and didn't have the most confidence," he said.

"It hasn't been easy this weekend, to be fair, and especially to keep my emotions flat. Definitely I have been a bit more tense than usual, also that played a big factor.

"But I try to enjoy the evening with family and friends and focus on tomorrow."

Hamilton said his pole, on his 43rd start for Ferrari, was "one of the greatest feelings".

It is not the first time he has qualified fastest for Ferrari - that was when he took sprint pole at the Chinese Grand Prix last year, in only his second race for the team.

But that was followed by a difficult debut season, when he looked a shadow of his former self, and was pretty much taken to the cleaners by Leclerc.

Hamilton's record is such that his performances last year left many perplexed - not least himself. He was consistently down on himself, even saying at one low point in the summer of 2025 that he was "just useless" and suggesting Ferrari should change drivers.

As this followed a similarly challenging final year for Mercedes, it inevitably led to questions about his future, whether age was catching up with him. After all, he had no explanations for his performances himself.

His form has improved this year, with a car that he finds much more to his liking, and he has a number of times referenced these perfectly valid questions. He did so again on Saturday.

"It's impossible to rank 105 pole positions," he said. "They have all been unique in their own way. It feels more special in this period where they're not every week and it's the first one with Ferrari in red.

"I've now had pole with three different teams, which is pretty phenomenal. And all the questions people had about whether a 40-year-old has still got it, there you go."

The battle between Hamilton and Leclerc has been much more even this year.

Hamilton leads his team-mate by eight points in the championship and in qualifying there is nothing to choose between them - it is now 12-10 in their head-to-head and Leclerc is ahead on average pace by just 0.037secs, when the gap was 0.15secs last year.

"I have been fortunate to have many great experiences with Mercedes over the years," said Hamilton. "We have had sprint pole but I have been really dreaming and eyeing for that first pole with the team.

"Charles is very, very quick over one lap. He has had an engineer he has worked with for years. It's an environment he is very aware of and used to.

"I am still settling in and learning, with new engineers this year. We have really found a good rapport and are really doing a great job. There is lots more to come, we just have to keep on at it, but what an amazing feeling to get that first."

Hamilton goes into the race with less knowledge than his rivals, a breakdown in second practice meaning he was not able to do his race-simulation run.

"It will will be a massive challenge to find the right balance but I am hopeful, it will be challenging and tough," he said.

For Antonelli, fourth is not such a bad place to start.

For one thing, he does not need any heroics. As long as he brings it home, he will become champion and fulfil a lifetime's ambition, as well as smash the record for the youngest-ever title winner by more than three years.

The run to the first corner in Mexico is long, more than 800m. Drivers on the second row have several times over the years used the slipstream to rocket into the lead.

Leclerc will be trying to do that, and the temptation may also be there for Antonelli. But the last thing he needs is to become embroiled in a first-corner pile-up.

The tension will doubtless still be there. But it's only a matter of time before it's released.

"Records are there to be broken, you know," said Hamilton, who described what Antonelli is achieving as "phenomenal".

"He's just got such a bright future ahead of him," added Hamilton. "I'm grateful that I can be racing in the time to see it, to witness it.

"I do hope in the future we get to have some actual battles because we didn't get to have any battles this year. It just flew past us on all the straights, more often than not.

"So, I hope next year that we're able to give him a bit more of a fight and get it really down to race craft. And, yeah, I'll be so happy for him."

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton says it's a 'dream' to emulate Michael Schumacher after claiming his first Ferrari pole at the Mexico City GP
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton became F1's oldest pole-sitter in 44 years after claiming his first Ferrari pole at the Mexico City Grand Prix; the result secured a record-extending 105th career pole for the Brit; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The 41-year-old unexpectedly snatched pole from Mercedes' George Russell in a thrilling end to qualifying to take his first pole in over three years and extend his record career pole tally to 105.

Hamilton and Schumacher share the sport's record for the most Drivers' Championships with seven each, but while the Brit won one title with McLaren and the other six with Mercedes, the bulk of Schumacher's success came at Ferrari as he won five in a row from 2000 to 2004.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 : "To get the pole, finally get a pole for Ferrari, just takes me back to when I was a kid and sitting on the sofa and watching Michael get those poles, thinking 'how cool would it be to do that?'"

"It was a dream my family have shared with me and I know so many people in the world grew up watching Michael.

"To be at this point of my career and still have this special feeling - 105 [poles], the number doesn't mean much in a sense, it feels like the first.

"I spoke a couple years ago about getting to have a first. It feels like when you get to 40 they are all gone, but I'm having those firsts this year and I'm in a really good place."

2009 F1 world champion and Hamilton's former team-mate Jenson Button said he noticed how confident the Ferrari driver looked in Q3.

Hamilton had been four tenths off the pace of his team-mate Charles Leclerc after the first runs in Q3, but then produced his best lap of the weekend when it mattered most.

"Watching that lap back, he was so smooth," Button said.

"There was one moment were he got a bit of oversteer but apart from that he is driving within the limits. I think that's the big positive."

Hamilton, who is the oldest pole-sitter since Mario Andretti in 1982, starts on the front row alongside Russell - the only two drivers who can prevent Kimi Antonelli from becoming world champion on Sunday.

Antonelli only needs to finish in the top nine to become champion but, should he come 10th or fail to score any points, victory for Hamilton or Russell would delay the inevitable for another round.

The long run down to Turn 1 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez always creates jeopardy and the pole-sitter has the disadvantage of towing trailing cars down the long straight.

Hamilton, whose only Grand Prix win for Ferrari came in Barcelona earlier this year, says it will be a "big challenge" to keep Russell and Leclerc behind, but that he will make his car "as wide as possible".

"It's a long run down to Turn 1 - very tough," he said.

"It's not a bad place to be in first but people can tow you. Lando did a really good job last year so I have to try and do what he did.

"Getting away off the line, I'm going in a little bit blind because in FP2 the engine stopped, so I didn't get to do a long run. I really don't know what the balance is like when you put all that fuel in.

"I kind of have to engineer my way through it and somehow drive my way through it. If we can get to Turn 1 first, then it comes down to how you manage your tyres. Hopefully we can have one of those special days where you can maybe whisper them a long way."

Russell thinks Turn 1 will be "crucial" as overtaking is likely to be difficult due to the high altitude, with the tight margins between the top teams potentially too small for passes to be possible later in the race.

"I think the race pace, there's probably going to be a tenth between the top seven or eight drivers," Russell said.

"Overtaking is going to be tough, overheating, etc. It's always the case here in Mexico. But get a good night's sleep and see what the race brings."

Leclerc added: "I'll keep my head down as much as possible and see what's possible. But, yes, it's always an exciting Turn 1 there, and we'll see how it goes."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes driver admits to feeling 'tense' amid effort to seal F1 title at Mexico City Grand Prix
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli needs top-nine finish to become world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix; he only qualified fifth and was off the pace compared to Mercedes team-mate George Russell; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The 20-year-old only needs to finish ninth in the race to become the sport's youngest world champion.

Antonelli qualified fifth on Saturday but will start from fourth on the grid due to a penalty for Max Verstappen.

Speaking after the session, the Italian revealed that he is not feeling his best as he continues to recover from an illness that caused him to miss his media duties on Thursday.

He told Sky Sports F1 : "It has not been the easiest weekend to be fair.

"Definitely still not feeling 100 per cent. There is talk of what could happen [with the championship] and definitely I'm a bit more tense than usual.

"Definitely I don't feel as relaxed but I try to have a good sleep tonight and focus on tomorrow."

Despite his condition, Antonelli was still able to produce a decent final lap in qualifying as he finished within two tenths of pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton.

However, the fact that his team-mate George Russell was only marginally behind Hamilton in second perhaps reflected the Italian not being able to summon his best level.

Antonelli added: "I struggled to get a good feeling from the tyres in Q3. I just didn't have the most confidence. I was a bit tense, I am not going to lie.

"It was a poor lap, many mistakes here and there. Overall, still P4 and a lot to play for tomorrow."

'It's insane!' - Norris happy to pass No 1 onto Antonelli

Lando Norris says he is "more than happy" to pass the number one he has had on his McLaren this year to Antonelli when the Mercedes driver replaces him as world champion.

Antonelli has massively exceeded expectations during just his second season in F1 to comprehensively outperform Russell, who began the year as the clear title favourite.

"He's done an incredible job and done it in a pretty incredible way," Norris said ahead of the race weekend in Mexico.

"People are saying he hasn't had any tough competition this year. That proves the point that he's done such an incredible job.

"He's got a very, very talented team-mate that he's beaten through the whole season.

"I have nothing but respect for Kimi. He's a very nice guy. We get along very well and I'm more than happy to pass the No 1 over to him.

"He deserves it. He's done an incredible job, especially in his second year in Formula 1. Youngest world champion, it's pretty insane.

"I enjoy other people having that kind of success. It's nice to see."

articles.title: Esteban Ocon: Haas driver denies 'physical violence' after being dropped by team for Mexico City Grand Prix
articles.summary: Haas replaced Esteban Ocon, who will leave team at end of season, with Ryo Hirakawa but did not specify why; Frenchman had been unhappy with decision to run him on medium tyres during a practice session on Friday; watch Sunday's Mexico City GP live on Sky Sports F1 at 8pm
articles.body:
Ocon, whose departure from the American-based squad at the end of the season had already been confirmed, was withdrawn without explanation on Saturday and replaced by Ryo Hirakawa, with Haas only confirming the one-time Grand Prix winner was not ill.

The Frenchman had been unhappy with his team's decision to run him in on medium tyres rather than softs during Friday's second practice session at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, saying "don't do this to me" to his race engineer Laura Mueller over team radio.

Ocon - victorious at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix when driving for Alpine - released a statement on Saturday, which read: "Following the recent decision from Haas F1 Team confirming that I will not be participating in this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, I wish to formally address some media reports and speculation surrounding the situation.

"Last night, a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved.

"Whilst I acknowledge that this took place, I categorically reject any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve differences of any nature.

"I strongly condemn violence in all its forms and firmly believe that disagreements should always be handled with professionalism, respect, and mutual understanding.

"I kindly ask that speculation be avoided while the matter is being addressed. Further updates will be communicated in due course."

There has been no indication as to whether Ocon - who has lost his seat to Brazilian Rafael Camara for 2027 - will drive for Haas at next weekend's Grand Prix in Brazil.

The 30-year-old has picked up seven points this season, 16 fewer than team-mate Oliver Bearman.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 during Saturday's final practice session in Mexico, Komatsu said of the Ocon incident: "I can't tell you much but I can tell you he's not ill.

"Honestly, the only thing I can say is we are focused on what's in front of us and getting Ryo in the best shape for qualifying."

Hirakawa, 32, qualified in 19th position as he become the oldest F1 debutant since André Lotterer for Caterham in 2014.

Button: Ocon may have thrown F1 career away

Reflecting on Ocon's statement, Sky Sports F1 pundit and former world champion Jenson Button said: "It's always difficult for a driver when you are out and your team are looking at someone else.

"But the best thing for him to do for number one, which is himself, is drive as hard as he can, works as hard as he can, and show how good he is.

"He can't do that anymore because of a disagreement on tyres in practice - it's not even qualifying or the race, it's practice.

"That frustrates me as these are 22 of the best drivers in the world. You don't get that opportunity easily and he has possibly thrown away the rest of his career in F1."

Sky Sports F1's David Croft had earlier said: "We don't know an awful lot. Haas are being tight-lipped.

"But talking behind the scenes, the relationship between Esteban and the team hasn't been magnificent in recent races.

"He wasn't happy with the tyre allocation runs yesterday and I think you can put two and two together and make four.

"It's a real shame because Ocon is a fine driver."

articles.title: Quiles se estrena como campeón igualando a Valentino Rossi
articles.standfirst: Máximo se escapa de una lucha en la que Pratama fue segundo y Carpe, tercero
articles.summary: Máximo se escapa de una lucha en la que Pratama fue segundo y Carpe, tercero
articles.body: Máximo Quiles ganó la carrera de Moto3 del Gran Premio de Malasia, en Sepang. El ya campeón estrenó esta condición a lo grande, logrando la undécima del curso, con lo que iguala a un tal Valentino Rossi, que lo hizo con 15 citas. Aún puede igualar el récord de 14 de David Alonso. El calor ya era alto, en el mediodía local, con 33 grados en el ambiente y hasta 47 en el asfalto, bajo el sol. En la salida, Quiles partía muy bien y controlaba desde su puesto en la pole. Almansa rebasaba a Danish en el primer ángulo y a Uriarte en el segundo, con un toque. Ríos se accidentaba; pudo regresar, pero sin visera; se acabó retirando. Almansa iba a la ofensiva y tardaba poco en adelantar a Quiles. Llegaban los primeros líos, con Carpe al alza, poniéndose segundo y con Brian a la baja, pues pasaba décimo por meta. Máximo intentaba pasar a Carpe, pero tenía un susto. Danish sacaba tajada pasando a los dos, con un rugido tremendo de la grada. Quiles reaccionaba al instante, rebasando a Carpe y Danish. Eso sí, entre tanta batalla, Almansa apretaba y cogía metros, a la par que los de detrás, con Pratama tirando, se arrimaban. Bertelle, que iba en ese grupo, se iba al suelo. El ya campeón, con gripe y todo, no permitía que el manchego se fugara; las grandes rectas y los rebufos, siempre hacen difícil una escapada en Sepang. El indonesio Pratama llegaba con los de arriba y superaba a Danish, en el pique asiático, pues Hakim replicaba al poco. David Muñoz intentaba no perder comba con los primeros y lo conseguía. En la quinta vuelta, Quiles ya adelantó a Almansa en el viraje de entrada a meta para liderar por primera vez. David Muñoz tenía un susto, que provocaba que dejara el grupo y fuera rebasado por Adrián Fernández y Kelso. Carpe veía el tirón de su paisano y rebasaba a Almansa, pero David replicaba en la curva 9. Esta batalla daba medio segundo a Quiles, que se iba abriendo por todas partes. Ogden, que buscaba puntuar, se caía. La carrera se rompía: Máximo abría hueco, Almansa quería liderar la persecución y los dos asiáticos podían con un Almansa que sufría. Carpe se enzarzaba en una lucha con Pratama y el murciano negaba, porque veía que Quiles se escapaba más en cada giro. Para colmo hasta Danish le tiraba la moto. Salmela se accidentaba. A falta de cinco vueltas, Quiles ya tenía más de dos segundos de renta. Bajaba la intensidad de los hachazos en el grupo, pero la distancia crecía. Kelso perdía el equilibrio en la curva 4. La batalla tardó poco en reactivarse, con pasadas continuas entre Danish, Pratama y Almansa; con Carpe a la expectativa hasta que restaron dos giros. El del Ajo KTM se ponía segundo en primer ángulo cuando encararon la última vuelta. Pratama le pasaba en la curva 4. En la siguiente, Danish hacía que Almansa se tuviera que abrir y perdiera sus opciones de podio. El malasio rebasó a Carpe, pero respondió en la 14, pero quedaba el final. Danish se tiró, pero se fue algo largo y Álvaro resistió para ganarse el podio y dejar sin cajón a Hakim. Por arriba, Máximo ganaba con una suficiencia abismal. Le da igual el calor, la gripe o lo que sea. Por lo pronto, ya ha ganado más carreras en la categoría pequeña que su mentor, Marc Márquez, pues llega a once. Máximo se acordaba de Phillip Island y de las víctimas del accidente ferroviario de Toledo. "Sabe muy bien. Estoy cabreado por Australia, porque tenía ritmo y podía haber peleado por otra victoria. Estuve enfermo todo el fin de semana y quería controlar las emociones, porque el triunfo va para los afectados por el accidente", decía. Carpe se lamentó de perder de vista a Quiles. "Tenía ritmo para irme con él, pero Almansa me pasó y me frenó", afirmó. David no estuvo tan cómodo. "No iba del todo bien, como otros días, pensé en el subcampeonato, el contacto con Danish me dejó sin opciones", comentó.
